draws.name: Nonresident white-tailed deer permit draw (archery, muzzleloader or firearm; one unit + one adjacent unit) incl. mule deer stamp
draws.quote: APPLICATION PERIOD: Applications for Non-Resident Deer Permits are open April 1 - April 24, 2026

draws.name: Resident firearm either-species/either-sex deer permit draw (East units 3,4,5,7,16 or West units 1,2,17,18)
draws.quote: Resident Firearms Either Species/Either Sex Firearms permits are available from May 12 - June 12, 2026 (available through resident draw only)

draws.name: Resident firearm and muzzleloader antelope draw
draws.quote: Applicants must apply online from May 12-June 12, 2026 or by phone 1-833-587-2164.

draws.name: Resident elk draw — Unit 2 / Sub-unit 2A (Fort Riley)
draws.quote: 2026 Resident Elk Permit Applications will be accepted from May 12-June 12, 2026

pointOnly.name: Resident firearm either-species deer preference point only
pointOnly.quote: Preference points can only be purchased during the application period.

pointOnly.name: Resident antelope preference point only
pointOnly.quote: Preference points can only be purchased May 12-June 12, 2026.

pointOnly.name: Resident elk bonus point only (Fort Riley draw)
pointOnly.quote: Bonus points can only be purchased during the application period.

fees.label: Nonresident deer application fee (inside the permit price)
fees.notes: CONFLICT: the deer page and fee schedule say the $475 permit includes a $25 application fee; KDWP's 13 Apr 2026 news release says $477.50 including a $27.50 application fee. Agent/transaction fees are extra.
fees.quote: includes $25 nonrefundable application fee (full permit fee only charged if applicant is drawn)

fees.label: Nonresident white-tailed deer permit, age 16+ (includes application fee)
fees.notes: Covers one white-tailed deer of either sex plus one antlerless whitetail. News release (https://www.ksoutdoors.gov/Home/Components/News/News/26/346) gives $477.50 instead. Youth (15 and under) permit $115.
fees.quote: Non-Resident White-tailed Deer Permit (age 16 and older) | $475.00 | available by draw only, application period April 1-24, 2026

fees.label: Nonresident mule deer stamp (random draw; Units 1, 2, 17, 18 archery/muzzleloader only)
fees.notes: In addition to the white-tailed deer permit. Preference points do not count toward the stamp draw.
fees.quote: Non-Resident Mule Deer Stamp | $150.00 | available by draw only, application period April 1-24, 2026

fees.label: Resident firearm either-species/either-sex deer permit (draw) — general resident
Resident deer preference point (firearm either-species permit)
fees.quote: may purchase a $10.00 preference point that will count toward a firearm either species, either sex deer permit

fees.label: Resident firearm/muzzleloader antelope permit (draw) — general resident
fees.notes: KDWP's antelope page labels these 'Application Fees'; the fee schedule lists them as permit fees. Landowner/tenant $35; youth $20; nonresident tenant $95.

fees.label: Resident antelope preference point
fees.notes: You cannot buy an antelope permit and a preference point in the same year.

fees.label: Resident elk application fee (also the bonus point fee)
fees.notes: CONFLICT: the elk page says $12.50; the fee schedule lists the elk preference point at $10.00.
fees.quote: Fee to apply for an elk permit or purchase a bonus point is $12.50.

fees.label: Resident any-elk permit (Fort Riley draw) — general resident
fees.notes: Collected from successful applicants only. Landowner/tenant $150; youth $125; nonresident tenant $300.

fees.label: Resident antlerless elk permit — general resident
Nonresident 1-year hunting license (age 16+) — must hold when applying
fees.quote: You will also need to possess a valid non-resident hunting license at the time of application, $125.00 (16 and over), $40.00 (15 and younger)

fees.label: Resident 1-year hunting license (ages 16-64)
fees.notes: Needed to hunt (residents 16-74 unless exempt); KDWP does not say it must be bought before applying.
fees.quote: 1 Year Hunting License | $25.00 | 365-day license, eligible for Auto Renew

prerequisites.text: Nonresidents must already hold a Kansas nonresident hunting license when they apply for a deer permit.
prerequisites.quote: possess a valid nonresident hunting license at the time of application

prerequisites.text: Hunter education certification for everyone born on or after July 1, 1957.
prerequisites.quote: All hunters (resident and nonresident) born on or after July 1, 1957 must be hunter‑education certified to hunt in Kansas.

prerequisites.text: Elk permits are for Kansas residents (and qualifying nonresident tenants) only.
prerequisites.quote: Only Kansas residents and qualifying nonresident tenants are eligible to obtain elk permits in Kansas.

prerequisites.text: Firearm and muzzleloader antelope permits are resident-only draws; nonresidents can only buy archery antelope over the counter.
prerequisites.quote: All firearm and muzzleloader antelope permits are issued through a lottery (draw) and are only available to Kansas residents.

notes: 2027 dates are not posted; all KDWP pages show the 2026 windows (nonresident deer April 1-24; resident deer/antelope/elk May 12-June 12). KDWP publishes no deadline time/time zone and no results date (news release: 'Applicants will be notified of draw results after the application period via email'). Fee conflicts: nonresident deer permit $475 incl. $25 app fee (deer page + fee schedule) vs $477.50 incl. $27.50 (13 Apr 2026 news release); elk app/bonus point $12.50 (elk page) vs $10 (fee schedule). Fees exclude agent/transaction fees. Access: ksoutdoors.gov returns 403 'Access Denied' to curl (and the old ksoutdoors.gov/Hunting/... fee page returned 403 to Node too), but current www.ksoutdoors.gov pages and the news release were served to a plain Node fetch with a browser User-Agent — no challenge was bypassed. KDWP regulation PDFs (K.A.R.) were not needed and not fetched.
